subject: Chemistry
topic: Why transition metals show variable oxidation states
title: One Element, Six Oxidation States: Why Transition Metals Vary
summary: The ns and (n−1)d electrons of a transition metal are close in energy, so both can take part in bonding. Manganese (3d⁵ 4s²) shows every state from +2 to +7; the most states occur in the middle of the series, Sc shows only +3 and Zn only +2, and the states change in steps of one.

notes.title: 06 – Why Transition Metals Show Variable Oxidation States

keyPoints: **ns and (n−1)d** electrons are close in energy, so **both take part in bonding**: variable oxidation states.
The **most** states occur **in the middle** of the series; **Sc only +3**, **Zn only +2**.
States differ **by one** (Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺); in the p-block usually **by two** (Sn²⁺/Sn⁴⁺).

blocks.p: Up to manganese, the highest oxidation state equals the number of 4s + 3d electrons: Sc +3, Ti +4, V +5, Cr +6, Mn +7.
Transition-metal states change one unit at a time (V +2, +3, +4, +5; Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺; Cu⁺/Cu²⁺). In the p-block the common states usually differ by two (Sn²⁺/Sn⁴⁺, Pb²⁺/Pb⁴⁺).
